notes: source.mutex.guard.v1: a typed-error exit taken while the invariant is open is refused at Q614 InvariantOpenAtErrorExit. The whole cascade is pinned, not only its head: the refused release leaves the guard live, which blocks the scope-exit destruction of the generation (Q619) and of the resource it parks (Q600 NonquiescentDestruction), and both survive into the end-of-trace sweep (Q600 OutstandingGuard, Q600 OutstandingMutex). Pinning all five entries is what shows the refusal did not silently release the guard. The `unless restored` half of the scenario is the restored.qr control, which closes the invariant before raising and is accepted. Q614 and Q613 stay distinct codes by design: the error path is attributed separately from the normal path, and the Lean theorem typed_error_exit_obeys_the_normal_release_rule proves both exits are subject to the same release rule. The control compiles through the Linux emission path, hence evidence_target=linux. Not established: the invariant predicate itself, which has no runtime representation and is carried as the InvariantPredicateDeclared premise.

controls.note: the same typed error raised after `close g;` checks, so Q614 is keyed to the open invariant and not to raising inside a critical section.
